question: On 26‑27 October 2026, the Council will decide on the Baltic Sea fishing quotas for 2027. The Commission’s proposal provides for drastic cuts to cod by-catches (by 88 % and 51 %) and an increase in sprat limits (by 44 %), which is causing serious concern within the sector. In light of the foregoing: 1.

How does the Council intend to modify the proposed reductions of 88 % and 51 % in cod by‑catches so that the EU-wide limits set out in the regulation do not lead to the complete shutdown of mixed fisheries?
How does the Council intend to take into account the negative socio-economic impacts on small-scale fleets and coastal communities when setting the final catch limits?

How does the Council assess the compatibility of the proposed 44 % increase in sprat catch limits with the obligation to apply an ecosystem-based approach and the overarching objective of rebuilding cod stocks?
